title: Laptop for Electrical and Electronics Engineering Students (2026): Specs for MATLAB, Altium, LTspice and Ansys Maxwell
summary: MATLAB R2026b wants 16 GB RAM and an SSD; Altium recommends 32 GB and runs on Windows only. Official specs of 8 EEE/ECE tools, Mac options, free licences.
body_markdown:
## Do you need a graphics card for electrical or ECE engineering?


**For the first two years, no.** MATLAB recommends a WebGL 2.0 GPU with 2 GB of memory for its graphics. LTspice, KiCad and STM32CubeIDE are light. The integrated graphics on a current Intel or AMD processor should handle this work.


You need a discrete card in two cases:


- **Altium Designer.** Altium's recommended card is a "high-performance graphics card (fully supporting DirectX 11 or better), such as GeForce GTX 1060/Radeon RX 470". That is a discrete card, not integrated graphics.
- **MATLAB GPU computing** (deep learning, large signal-processing jobs). MathWorks supports "NVIDIA GPU architectures with compute capability 7.5 to 12.x". Compute capability is NVIDIA's version number for a GPU generation. Every GeForce RTX laptop GPU from the RTX 20 series onward meets it, per NVIDIA's[CUDA GPU list](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus) . MathWorks' GPU page lists only NVIDIA, and on a Mac GPU acceleration is not available.


Ansys lists "professional workstation class 3-D" graphics as the minimum for Electronics Desktop Student. That is the only tool here that names a workstation card. The student version caps HFSS and Maxwell models at 64,000 mesh elements, so the models you can build with it are small.


## Can you use a MacBook for electrical or ECE engineering?


**Much more than in mechanical or civil engineering.** MATLAB and Simulink, LTspice, KiCad and STM32CubeIDE all run natively on macOS. That covers circuits, signals, control systems and most embedded labs.

There are catches:


- **MATLAB on Mac is Apple silicon only.** MathWorks says R2025b was the last release for Intel Macs. On a Mac, "GPU acceleration with Parallel Computing Toolbox is not available".
- **Altium Designer is Windows only, and a virtual machine does not help.** Altium says "running Altium Designer on virtual machines and emulators is not supported", so Parallels is not an official route. KiCad is the PCB tool that works on a Mac.
- **Ansys Electronics Desktop Student** lists Windows, and **Vivado** ships only Windows and Linux installers. FPGA and electromagnetic work means a college lab PC or a Windows laptop.


So: if your syllabus is circuits, MATLAB and microcontrollers, a MacBook with 16 GB works. If you plan to specialise in PCB design, FPGA or electric-machine design, buy Windows.


## Which electrical engineering software is free for students?


Tool Student access (checked 19 Nov 2026)


**LTspice** Free for everyone. Analog Devices calls it "Fast, Free, Unlimited".


**KiCad** Free and open source under the GNU GPL v3, on Windows, macOS and Linux.


**Altium Designer** Altium Student Lab: free licence, "valid for 1 year and can be renewed yearly as long as you remain a student". Windows only.


**Ansys Electronics Desktop Student** Free for verified students (SheerID, renewed yearly); built-in licence valid until 31 July 2027. Limits: 64,000 3D mesh elements, 50 Circuit components, 4 cores.


**MATLAB and Simulink** Free if your college has a Campus-Wide Licence; otherwise the paid Student Suite. Details in our guide:[is MATLAB free for students?](https://resources.skill-lync.com/articles/is-matlab-free-for-students/)


**AMD Vivado** From the 2026.1 release, a free Basic licence tier, aimed at Spartan UltraScale+ FPGAs.


**PSCAD Free Edition** Free; "fully featured and limited only by network size and a few other non-essential features".


The practical result: you can put a full circuit, PCB and electromagnetics toolkit on your own laptop for free. LTspice, KiCad, Altium and Ansys Electronics Desktop Student cost nothing. Only MATLAB may cost money, and many Indian colleges already pay for it.


## Recommended laptop specs for electrical and ECE students


We deliberately do not quote rupee prices. Configurations, GST and sales move them every few weeks. Buy against these specs instead.


### Tier 1: 1st and 2nd year (MATLAB, Simulink basics, LTspice, KiCad, Arduino and STM32)


- **CPU:** 4 cores or more **with AVX2** (Intel Core i5/Core Ultra 5 or AMD Ryzen 5).
- **RAM:** **16 GB** , upgradable if possible.
- **GPU:** integrated graphics are fine.
- **Storage:** **512 GB SSD.** MathWorks "strongly" recommends an SSD.
- **OS:** Windows 11, or a MacBook with Apple silicon if you accept the limits above.


### Tier 2: 3rd and 4th year (Altium PCB projects, Simulink power electronics and EV models, Ansys Maxwell)


- **CPU:** Intel Core i7/Core Ultra 7 or AMD Ryzen 7. Altium recommends "Intel Core i7 12th Generation (Alder Lake) or later processor or equivalent".
- **RAM:** **32 GB** (Altium's recommendation).
- **GPU:** discrete, GeForce GTX 1060 class or better (Altium's recommendation). An NVIDIA RTX card also covers MATLAB GPU computing.
- **Storage:** **1 TB SSD.** A full MATLAB install is 25 GB, Ansys Electronics Desktop Student needs 17 GB and Altium 10 GB, before any projects.
- **OS:** **Windows 11.** Altium recommends it and does not support virtual machines.


### Tier 3: deep learning, FPGA and large simulations


- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX with as much video memory as you can afford, for MATLAB GPU computing and deep learning.
- **RAM:** 32 GB or more.
- **OS:** Windows or Linux. Vivado has no macOS version.


## What to check before you pay


- **Your syllabus.** Power systems, machines and EV electives lean on MATLAB/Simulink. VLSI and embedded electives add Vivado and STM32CubeIDE. PCB design adds Altium or KiCad.
- **AVX2 on the processor.** Search the exact chip with "AVX2".
- **Upgradable RAM.** Search the exact model number with "RAM slots". Soldered 16 GB cannot grow.
- **Windows 11 if you want Altium.** Altium recommends Windows 11, and says running it with Windows 11's Smart App Control enabled is not supported.
- **A 1920 x 1080 screen or better.** KiCad recommends 1920 x 1080; Altium's minimum is 1680 x 1050 and it recommends dual 2560 x 1440 monitors.
